task.name: Nothing re-evaluates existing issues when shape policy changes, so labels stamped under superseded rules stay applied
task.story_text:
## Summary

When shape-policy code changes on `main`, nothing re-evaluates issues that already exist. The Action reconciles a label when the *issue* changes; no path reconciles when the *rules* change. Labels stamped under superseded rules stay applied until someone edits the body.

ADR-0003 clause 1 makes the Action authoritative for ambient label state, reflecting "is this issue in shape today?". A sweep is what makes that claim true after a policy change.

## Example

`5250d407` promoted `no_observable_done_state` from `ADVISORY` to `BLOCKING` on 2026-08-21. Issues #2601, #2600 and #2230 had been evaluated the previous day and carried no `needs-grooming` label. Their bodies were never edited, so nothing re-ran, and the labels were wrong until reconciled by hand. The repo currently has 131 open issues against rules that have moved repeatedly since April.

Desired shape of the preview output:

```
shape-check sweep — preview (131 open issues)
  + needs-grooming  #2601  no_observable_done_state
  + needs-grooming  #2600  no_observable_done_state
  - needs-grooming  #2408  (now runnable)
128 unchanged
```

## Acceptance criteria

- A sweep entrypoint evaluates every open issue and reports the set of label and comment changes it would make, without writing anything.
- The same entrypoint applies those changes when asked, writing only where the label or bot comment differs from the computed result, so a second consecutive run reports zero changes.
- Pull requests touching shape-policy code print the resulting delta in CI.
- The sweep runs against `main` after such a pull request merges.
- An operator can trigger preview or apply manually.
- Each bot comment records the shape-policy digest that produced its verdict, and that digest is unchanged by commits which do not alter policy.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] GitHub issue pagination is malformed for documented /repositories links, so the sweep cannot cover repositories with more than 100 open issues. | [anthropic-opus-cli] Sweep/reconciliation layer is well-built and meets five of six criteria, but the new tracking-label removal branch strips an operator-applied epic label and breaks the second-run-zero-changes guarantee for superseded epics.

findings.description: When GitHub returns a paginated issue Link URL under /repositories, the sweep builds the next request as a repository-relative path under /repos/<owner>/<repo>, so page 2 of the issue listing is requested from the wrong endpoint and the sweep cannot cover repositories with more than 100 open issues.

Reconciliation now removes the configured tracking label (epic) from any open issue whose computed shape is not tracking-only, which for an epic-labelled issue that also declares itself superseded deletes the operator-applied label and changes the reason set the next evaluation produces, so the following consecutive sweep rewrites that issue's bot comment instead of reporting zero changes.

The policy manifest is a hardcoded list of filenames read at runtime with no guard that each file still exists, so renaming or splitting a policy module makes every issue-event run raise FileNotFoundError while the workflow path filter silently stops matching the moved code.

The apply sweep creates a bot comment on every open issue that lacks one, so the first run against a backlog of roughly 131 issues posts a comment on each with no cap or staged rollout, generating a notification per issue.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Steps 2 and 6 cover pagination of open issues but not comments. HttpGitHubAPI.list_comments() in src/theforge/shape_check/action.py currently reads only the first 100 comments, so a marker beyond that page would be missed and repeated apply runs could create duplicate comments instead of reporting zero changes.
  Suggestion: Paginate list_comments until exhaustion and add a sweep regression test where the existing bot-owned marker appears on the second page.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 (PR preview must read repository issues) is only partially retired. Preview-only + no write permissions resolves the safety half, but the plan does not settle whether the PR job's token can list issues — a fork-originated pull_request run gets a read-only token and, depending on repo default permissions, may need an explicit issues: read in the job's permissions block or it will fail with 403 rather than printing a delta (AC 3).

finding_registry.description: When GitHub returns a paginated issue Link URL under /repositories, the sweep builds the next request as a repository-relative path under /repos/<owner>/<repo>, so page 2 of the issue listing is requested from the wrong endpoint and the sweep cannot cover repositories with more than 100 open issues.

Reconciliation now removes the configured tracking label (epic) from any open issue whose computed shape is not tracking-only, which for an epic-labelled issue that also declares itself superseded deletes the operator-applied label and changes the reason set the next evaluation produces, so the following consecutive sweep rewrites that issue's bot comment instead of reporting zero changes.

The policy manifest is a hardcoded list of filenames read at runtime with no guard that each file still exists, so renaming or splitting a policy module makes every issue-event run raise FileNotFoundError while the workflow path filter silently stops matching the moved code.

The apply sweep creates a bot comment on every open issue that lacks one, so the first run against a backlog of roughly 131 issues posts a comment on each with no cap or staged rollout, generating a notification per issue.
The paginated request helper follows any absolute URL taken from a response Link header, including a plaintext http:// URL, and attaches the bearer token to that request.
The sweep report helper still carries a '(no longer tracking)' summary branch for a tracking-label removal that reconciliation no longer emits, so the branch can never render.

When a pagination Link header points at a host or scheme other than the configured GitHub API endpoint, the paginated reader stops and returns the pages collected so far without emitting any log line, so a partial issue listing is indistinguishable from a complete one.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Add a deterministic policy digest and a reusable reconciliation diff layer, then expose it through the existing shape-check module entrypoint for preview/apply sweeps. Wire the same entrypoint into the current shape-check workflow for issue events, PR previews, post-merge apply runs, and manual operator dispatch.

steps.description: Define the shape-policy digest boundary and include it in bot comments
steps.details: Create a stdlib-only digest helper that hashes an explicit manifest of policy-affecting shape_check source files used by the current verdict path, such as check.py, heuristics.py, issue_spec.py, diagnosis_spec.py, parsing.py, placeholders.py, _mapping.py, verdict.py, classifier.py, and types.py. Thread the computed digest into render_comment output while preserving COMMENT_MARKER and existing bot-comment lookup behavior; update action tests to assert the digest line is present and unchanged when unrelated files change.

steps.description: Add pure sweep planning that computes label and comment deltas without writing
steps.details: Extract the existing desired-state calculations from run_action into reusable pure comparison logic: for each open issue, call the existing check(title, body, labels), compute desired needs-grooming/tracking label state and desired bot comment body including the digest, compare against current labels and find_bot_comment output, and return structured pending changes plus an unchanged count. Keep the GitHub API boundary stdlib-only and extend it only as needed to read paginated open issues, excluding pull requests from /issues results.

steps.description: Implement preview and apply modes for the sweep entrypoint
steps.details: Route python -m theforge.shape_check so the existing issues.opened/edited behavior remains the default for issue events, and add a sweep mode selected by argv or environment for preview/apply. Preview must print a stable summary like '+ needs-grooming #2601 reason_codes', '- needs-grooming #2408 (now runnable)', and comment create/update lines without API writes. Apply must perform only the computed missing label/comment operations, so replaying apply immediately reports zero changes.

steps.description: Preserve single-issue Action behavior on opened/edited events
steps.details: Keep run_action as the event reconciler and have it use the same desired-state/comment rendering path as sweep. Existing tests for label application, label removal, tracking label application, superseded behavior, and update-in-place comments should continue to pass with only digest-related expectation updates.

steps.description: Wire CI, post-merge, and manual workflow triggers
steps.details: Extend shape-check.yml with pull_request preview runs filtered to the explicit policy file manifest, push-to-main apply runs with the same paths filter, and workflow_dispatch inputs for preview/apply. Keep issue opened/edited handling intact. Use the same install and python -m theforge.shape_check invocation in all cases, with write permissions only for issue events, apply mode, and manual apply.

steps.description: Add workflow and idempotency regression coverage
steps.details: Cover preview as no-write, apply as write-only-on-diff, second apply as zero-change, digest-driven comment updates, open issue pagination/exclusion of PRs, and workflow trigger/path/input wiring by loading the committed YAML as existing workflow tests do.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A sweep entrypoint evaluates every open issue and reports the set of label and comment changes it would make, without writing anything.
The same entrypoint applies those changes when asked, writing only where the label or bot comment differs from the computed result, so a second consecutive run reports zero changes.
Pull requests touching shape-policy code print the resulting delta in CI.
The sweep runs against main after such a pull request merges.
An operator can trigger preview or apply manually.
Each bot comment records the shape-policy digest that produced its verdict, and that digest is unchanged by commits which do not alter policy.

risks.description: The spec does not define the exact boundary of shape-policy code.
risks.mitigation: Make the boundary explicit in the digest helper and reuse that same manifest for workflow path filters, so digest invalidation and CI triggering cannot drift.

risks.description: Pull request preview needs to evaluate candidate policy code while reading repository issues.
risks.mitigation: Use preview-only behavior on pull_request, keep write permissions out of PR runs, and document any GitHub token limitations in workflow comments rather than switching to unsafe pull_request_target execution.

risks.description: Existing bot comments lack a digest, so the first sweep after deployment will update otherwise unchanged comments.
risks.mitigation: Treat missing digest as a comment diff in preview/apply; after one apply run, subsequent runs are idempotent because the rendered comment body matches.
